commentary_segments.text: The current source of a differential pair has both an output resistance R and B capacitance C . Its size B depends mainly on the Drain-Bulk capacitance C DB of the current source transistor. Its value is close to that of the C of that transistor GS (as explained in Chapter 1). This capacitance C also B includes the capacitance C between the well, in well,bulk which both input transistors are imbedded, and the substrate. It can therefore be a lot larger than the C of the current source transistor. GS As a result, a new break frequency f shows up. It occurs as a zero in the characteristic of the B gain A , but as a pole in one of the CMRR. Calculation of this frequency depends on the values dc of these different capacitances. It will be somewhere between the dominant pole of the amplifier and a fraction of the f frequency of the current source transistor. A small square device is optimal, most probably requiring a high value of V −V , which is good for its f as well! GS T T

This capacitance C also B includes the capacitance C between the well, in well,bulk which both input transistors are imbedded, and the substrate. It will be somewhere between the dominant pole of the amplifier and a fraction of the f frequency of the current source transistor.
